# clickhouse_clickpipes_ssh_key (Resource)

You can use the `clickhouse_clickpipes_ssh_key` resource to create a standalone, service-scoped SSH key resource for ClickPipes.

The server generates an Ed25519 keypair and returns the OpenSSH `public_key`. Install that public key in your bastion's `authorized_keys` so that ClickPipes can tunnel through it. The private key never leaves ClickHouse Cloud.

Once created, reference the resource from a ClickPipe source via its `ssh_key_resource_id` attribute (supported on Kafka, Postgres, MySQL, and MongoDB sources) instead of providing inline SSH configuration. A reference is mutually exclusive with inline SSH config and is immutable on the pipe; changing it forces the pipe to be recreated.

The resource lifecycle is:

- `pending` — created, connectivity not yet validated.
- `active` — the last connectivity validation succeeded.
- `failed` — the last connectivity validation failed.

All attributes (`name`, `description`, `host`, `port`, `username`) are immutable; changing any of them forces resource replacement — the public API exposes no update operation for SSH key resources.

~> **Note:** Connectivity validation requires the public key to already be installed on the bastion, so it is a day-2 operation performed out of band and is not run automatically when the resource is created.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "clickhouse_clickpipes_ssh_key" "bastion" {
  service_id  = "3a10a385-ced2-452e-abb8-908c80976a8f"
  name        = "production-bastion"
  description = "Bastion for the prod VPC"
  host        = "bastion.example.com"
  port        = 22
  username    = "clickpipes"
}

# The server generates the keypair; install the returned public key on the
# bastion's authorized_keys so ClickPipes can tunnel through it.
output "bastion_public_key" {
  value = clickhouse_clickpipes_ssh_key.bastion.public_key
}

# Reference the SSH key resource from a ClickPipe source instead of inline SSH config.
resource "clickhouse_clickpipe" "postgres_via_bastion" {
  service_id = "3a10a385-ced2-452e-abb8-908c80976a8f"
  name       = "postgres-cdc"

  source = {
    postgres = {
      host                = "10.0.0.5"
      port                = 5432
      database            = "app"
      ssh_key_resource_id = clickhouse_clickpipes_ssh_key.bastion.id

      # ... remaining Postgres source configuration ...
    }
  }

  # ... destination, scaling, etc. ...
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) Hostname or IP address of the SSH bastion. Immutable; changing it forces resource replacement.
- `name` (String) Name of the SSH key resource. Unique per service and immutable; changing it forces resource replacement.
- `service_id` (String) The ID of the ClickHouse service this SSH key resource belongs to
- `username` (String) Username to authenticate with on the SSH bastion. Immutable; changing it forces resource replacement.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the SSH key resource. Immutable; changing it forces resource replacement (the public API has no update operation for SSH key resources).
- `port` (Number) Port of the SSH bastion. Defaults to 22. Immutable; changing it forces resource replacement.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the SSH key resource was created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the SSH key resource
- `last_validated_at` (String) Timestamp of the last connectivity validation, if any.
- `public_key` (String) The OpenSSH public key generated by the server. Install this in the bastion's `authorized_keys` before validating connectivity.
- `status` (String) Validation lifecycle status of the SSH key resource (pending, active, or failed).
- `status_message` (String) Human-readable detail about the current status, e.g. the reason a validation failed.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the SSH key resource was last updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# ClickPipes SSH key resources can be imported by specifying both service ID and SSH key resource ID.
terraform import clickhouse_clickpipes_ssh_key.example xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx:xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```
